topics.label: Fed & Macro
topics.covers: The Fed (decisions, minutes, speeches by the Chair, governors and regional presidents, balance sheet), other major central banks when they move markets (ECB, BoJ, BoE), and the US data calendar: CPI, PCE, payrolls/unemployment, GDP, retail sales, ISM, jobless claims, consumer sentiment and inflation expectations.
topics.lens: How a rates desk reads it: what was expected vs. what happened, what it does to the path of policy (what futures now price), and what it means for the front end of the curve and the dollar.
queries: US economic data today CPI PCE jobs report
ECB Bank of Japan Bank of England decision

topics.label: Markets & Earnings
topics.covers: Cross-asset moves of the day: Treasuries and the yield curve, equities (S&P 500, Nasdaq, sectors), credit spreads, the dollar and major FX pairs, oil and gold as macro assets, volatility (VIX/MOVE). Market-moving earnings (megacap tech, big banks, bellwethers) and the themes behind them (AI capex, consumer health).
topics.lens: What moved, why, and whether the move is signal or noise. Always connect a price move to a driver; note positioning and what's priced in.
queries: stock market today close S&P 500 Nasdaq
credit spreads high yield investment grade

topics.label: Policy & Geopolitics
topics.covers: Fiscal policy and Treasury issuance, tariffs and trade, elections, regulation that hits markets (bank capital, SEC), sovereign debt stress abroad, wars, sanctions and shipping chokepoints — only through the market-impact lens.
topics.lens: Skip the politics-as-sport. Ask: what does this change for growth, inflation, deficits, risk premia or a specific asset? Who wins and who loses in markets?
queries: Iran Strait of Hormuz oil shipping latest
sovereign bond yields France UK Japan

topics.label: Energy
topics.covers: Sector coverage, by subsector: (1) Upstream/E&Ps and oil majors (Exxon, Chevron, shale, OPEC+ quotas, rig counts); (2) Midstream and pipelines (MLPs, export terminals, tanker rates, Hormuz flows); (3) Refining and products (crack spreads, gasoline/diesel, turnarounds); (4) Natural gas and LNG (Henry Hub, TTF/JKM, export capacity); (5) Oilfield services (SLB, Halliburton, Baker Hughes); (6) Power and utilities (data-center load growth, PJM capacity prices, grid and transmission, nuclear/SMRs); (7) Renewables, storage and the transition (solar, wind, batteries, uranium, coal); (8) Energy M&A and capex.
topics.lens: How an energy-sector analyst or commodities trader reads it: supply/demand balance, inventories, curve structure (backwardation/contango), and which equities or credits are exposed.

topics.label: Industrials
topics.covers: Sector coverage, by subsector: (1) Aerospace and defense (Boeing, Lockheed, RTX, GE Aerospace, defense budgets); (2) Machinery and capital goods (Caterpillar, Deere, Eaton, electrical equipment); (3) Transports (rails, trucking, airlines, shipping, freight volumes); (4) Infrastructure and construction (engineering and construction, building products, aggregates and cement, grid and transmission build-out, data-center construction, federal infrastructure spending); (5) Reshoring, tariffs and supply chains; (6) The industrial cycle (ISM, orders, capex, capacity utilization); and industrials earnings.
topics.lens: Where we are in the industrial cycle and who's exposed: order books, margins, pricing power, and how macro (rates, tariffs, defense budgets) flows through to the sector.
queries: electrical equipment grid Eaton GE Vernova

topics.label: The World
topics.covers: Major international news in the style of a newspaper's world section: wars and ceasefires, diplomacy and summits, elections and changes of government abroad, coups and protests, disasters and humanitarian crises, and big moves by China, Russia, Europe, the Middle East, India, Latin America and Africa. Cover the most important 2–4 world stories of the day even when they aren't market stories.
topics.lens: Be the reader's world-news briefing so they can talk about current events with anyone: what happened, why it matters, and the background to understand it. Add one line on market relevance only when there genuinely is some (oil, FX, sovereign bonds, sanctions); leave market-driven geopolitics to the Policy beat.
